title: Pip's Rainy Day Box
checkpoint: Phase 1 (Introduction) — a wordless story for sharing and talking through together; there are no sounds to decode yet.
note_for_grown_ups: A simple, true kind of play: making something new out of bits and pieces found lying around. Ask what your child might make from a rainy-day box of their own.

pages.talk_prompt: It is raining outside the barn — what do you think Pip could do on a day like this?
pages.illustration: Pip the sparrow looking out through an old barn window at grey rain falling outside.

pages.talk_prompt: Pip has found a piece of string on the barn floor — what do you think he will do with it?
pages.illustration: Pip the sparrow hopping across straw-covered barn floorboards, picking up a short length of brown string.

pages.talk_prompt: Pip has found a few more little things — can you see what they are?
pages.illustration: Pip the sparrow dropping a small round button and a twist of golden straw into a little open tin.

pages.talk_prompt: Pip is arranging his found treasures — what do you think he is making?
pages.illustration: Pip the sparrow arranging the brown string, button and golden straw carefully inside the little tin.

pages.talk_prompt: Pip is putting it all together — what has he made?
pages.illustration: Pip the sparrow carefully tying the straw and string into a tiny sailboat shape with the button as a wheel.

pages.talk_prompt: Pip looks very pleased with his rainy-day project — how do you think he feels?
pages.illustration: Pip the sparrow admiring his finished tiny straw sailboat on the barn windowsill while rain patters on the roof outside.
